correctness.rationale: The incidence list defines the Fano plane and its 21-edge bipartite graph. Under iid continuous priorities the survivor-order argument makes the next legal edge uniform. A candidate output M must be a maximal matching, and it occurs iff every non-M edge is later than some incident M edge: necessity follows from rejection; sufficiency follows by scanning in order, as selected edges are disjoint and all others have an earlier selected neighbor. For a fixed order of the k selected edges and conditional on their priority values, each nonselected edge independently contributes the survival factor for its earliest incident selected edge. Summing simplex integrals covers the entire joint cube for the selected values without any extra k! factor. Reversing u to 1-u gives exactly the nested denominators j plus the sum of the last j rejection exponents. An independently written vertex-recursion enumeration and exact rational weight calculation reproduced all 234 matchings and the five (size, multiplicity, weight) triples: (5,42,19/13860), (6,28,261/98560), (6,56,8257/1995840), (6,84,91723/23950080), (7,24,1247/95040). Their size masses are 19/330, 497/792, 1247/3960; mean 24779/3960. The normalization, uniform perfect fraction 24/234 and perfect-output ratio 16211/5280 follow exactly.
residual_risks: Independence and uniform rank order matter; the calculation verifies the specified single-round edge process only. Probability classes here do not by themselves certify the automorphism-orbit classification of the comparison record.
